why: I checked each of the 7 verifier checks against its expect line. Checks 1–5 compare the output byte for byte with cmp against the exact expected text plus a newline. Only check 1 also requires exit=0, which its line demands. Check 5 keeps the JSON backslash-t literal with printf '%s', matching the line. Check 6 PASS needs npm test to exit 0 and a test in test/ that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab input and asserts on the output. Its FAIL examples (comment-only, no tabs, no assertion) only spell out those words. Check 7 needs an example --tsv invocation and that README "documents what the flag does", which is a fair reading of "documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation". `table.tsv` appears only "for example", not as required wording. The stricter ideas (flag position, whether the tests catch removed --tsv handling, out-of-scope changes) all sit under "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)".
